chunks: As for what Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Ja'far, from his father, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon them all), who said:

Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'When a man claps his hands in confirmation of a sale, the sale becomes binding, even if they have not yet separated.' This does not contradict what we previously stated, that separation by bodies is what necessitates the sale, because what this report necessitates is that clapping in confirmation of the sale, without separation, is a cause for the sale to be binding. The meaning of this is that it is a cause for the permissibility of ownership, provided that they separate by bodies and do not annul the contract while they are still in the same place. The earlier reports indicated that they have the option (to annul) as long as they have not separated by annulling the concluded contract. And his saying 'even if they have not separated' may mean if they have not separated by a distant separation or a specific separation, because the amount that necessitates the sale is something small, even if it is the distance of a step, for the sale becomes binding by it. And on this basis, there is no contradiction between the reports.

key_terms.صَفْقَة: Act of confirmation or clapping hands to seal a deal

ai.seo_question: What makes a sale binding in Shia fiqh: physical separation or an act of confirmation?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent contradiction between hadiths requiring physical separation (iftiraq) and those validating immediate binding via confirmation (safqa) by interpreting 'separation' as a minimal distance sufficient to prevent immediate retraction. This interpretation preserves the principle of khayar al-majlis (the right of option while in the meeting place), allowing parties to annul the contract before they physically part ways. The text highlights the nuanced juristic reasoning used to harmonize conflicting narrations regarding the precise moment a sale becomes irrevocable.
